marks.gloss_en: כמאן? כי האי תנא, דתנן: ...רבי אליעזר מחייב קרן וחומש ורבי יהושע פוטר -- date honey is not the fruit itself
the mishnah: date honey, apple wine, winter-grape vinegar and other fruit juices of teruma -- R' Eliezer obligates [a non-priest who drank them] in the principal and a fifth
מתיב רב יוסף: ושוין שבוחשין את השתות בשבת ושותין זיתום המצרי -- ואי סלקא דעתך לרפואה קא מכוין, רפואה בשבת מי שרי?!
the baraita: and they agree that one may stir shetita on Shabbat and drink Egyptian zithom
ואת לא תסברא? והא תנן: כל האוכלין אוכל אדם לרפואה בשבת (= p_kol_haochlin_lirfua) -- what you must say there, the man intends eating; here too the man intends eating (= p_gavra_laachila_mechaven)
the mishnah: all foods a person may eat for healing on Shabbat, and all drinks he may drink
לישנא אחרינא: he intends eating and the healing comes of itself; so too here (= p_refua_mimeila)
Abaye, the other version: the man intends eating and the healing comes of itself; so too here
והלכתא: תמרי ועבדינהו טרימא מברכין עלייהו בורא פרי העץ
Rava: certainly you mean something pounded
R' Yehuda: if he made them thick, they are obligated
Mar Zutra made his meal on it and blessed over it 'Who brings forth bread from the earth'
Mar bar Rav Ashi: a person fulfils his [matza] obligation on Pesach with them
Mar bar Rav Ashi: over date honey one blesses 'by Whose word all things came to be'
one of the Rabbis to Rava: terima -- what is its law? (Rava did not grasp the word; Ravina asked the asker: do you mean sesame, safflower or grape-pit terima?)
shetita: Rav said 'by Whose word all things came to be'
Rav Chisda: they do not disagree -- this [Shmuel's] is of thick shetita

Rav and Shmuel's statement is needed: from the baraita alone I would say [blessing only where] one intends eating and healing comes of itself; here, intending healing from the outset, one would not bless at all
ורבנן? -- and the Rabbanan: what of 'who brings you out from under the burdens of Egypt' (Ex 6:7), which R' Nechemya reads as 'brings out'?

ההוא הכי קאמר -- God tells Israel: when I bring you out I will do something so you know it was I who brought you out; in 'and you shall know... hamotzi' the bringing-out is already past (= p_vidatem_afik)

that verse means: the Holy One said to Israel -- when I bring you out, I will do something for you so that you will know that it is I who brought you out of Egypt ('and you shall know that I am the Lord your God, hamotzi')

זה הוא שאומרים עליו דאדם גדול הוא ובקי בברכות הוא?! בשלמא אי אמר המוציא... אלא דאמר מוציא מאי קא משמע לן? -- is this the expert in blessings? 'hamotzi' would have taught the meaning and the halakha; 'motzi' teaches nothing
the Rabbanan praised the son of Rav Zevid to R' Zeira: he is a great man and expert in blessings
over bread one says 'hamotzi lechem min haaretz'
דכתיב אל מוציאם ממצרים -- 'motzi' here speaks of a completed bringing-out
דכתיב המוציא לך מים מצור החלמיש -- the Rabbanan's verse, as Rava gives it
שנאמר המוציא אתכם מתחת סבלות מצרים -- R' Nechemya's verse, as Rava gives it
